chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Hafs, and one or more of our companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
He was asked about the man who swears by his brother. He said: 'There is nothing upon him; he merely intended to honour him'.

key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ: there is nothing upon him (no obligation/expitation)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on swearing an oath by a person, such as a brother, and is expiation required?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that swearing by a brother is a common idiom of respect rather than a binding vow, thus exempting the speaker from expiation (kaffarah). This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of prioritizing the speaker's intention (niyyah) and linguistic context over the literal wording of the oath. It underscores the flexibility in Islamic law regarding casual oaths used for emphasis or honorific purposes.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Hafs, and someone else from our companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,
‘He<sup>asws</sup> was asked about the man who swore upon his brother. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is nothing upon him. But rather he intended to honour him’.
en.sarwar: 12. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from ibn Faddal from Hafs and from more than one person of our people who has narrated the following: “Once abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
was asked about the case of a man who swears by his brother. He (the Imam) said, ‘It does not have any valid effect on him; he only wanted to honor and respect him.’”
